backlog.spec: In predict's tta function change UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE from 0.25 to 0.15 to cut the time spent on 6-view TTA at test time. Accuracy may drop slightly; check the net cost.
backlog.title: Drop TTA quantile to 15%

backlog.spec: Change UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE from 0.25 to 0.4 so more test images get multi-view averaging. This tests whether the accuracy gain outweighs the extra time.
backlog.title: Raise TTA quantile to 40%

backlog.spec: In CifarLoader.__iter__ skip batch_crop and use the unpadded flipped images when self.epoch >= 6 (the last ~1.5 epochs). Less augmentation at the end of training can raise final accuracy.
backlog.title: No translation in final epochs

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE=2048. Multiply MUON_LR by 1.15, and HEAD_LR and BIAS_LR by 1.2. This gives fewer optimizer steps and better GPU utilisation. Keep EPOCHS unchanged.
backlog.title: Batch 2048 with scaled LRs

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE=1024 and scale all learning rates by about 0.85. Set EPOCHS to 7.0 to offset the extra per-step overhead.
backlog.title: Batch 1024 with fewer epochs

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 remove the third unrolled iteration (the A, B, X update) so only 2 iterations run. This saves optimizer time. Check whether accuracy holds.
backlog.title: Two Newton-Schulz iterations

backlog.spec: Change MUON_MOMENTUM from 0.655 to 0.75 and lower MUON_LR from 0.205 to 0.18 to compensate for the larger effective step.
backlog.title: Muon momentum 0.75

backlog.spec: Replace lr_factor2 with a schedule that warms up linearly from 0.2 to 1.0 over the first 3 steps, then decays linearly to zero. Apply it to all param groups.
backlog.title: Short LR warmup

backlog.spec: Change lr_factor2 to (1 - step/total_train_steps)**1.3 so the decay is steeper early and gentler late. Keep the other settings.
backlog.title: Convex LR tail

backlog.spec: Disable color jitter (set enabled False) to skip the compiled jitter kernel and save time. Check whether the accuracy loss is small.
backlog.title: Remove color jitter

backlog.spec: Reduce LABEL_SMOOTHING from 0.09 to 0.06. Shorter training may prefer less smoothing.
backlog.title: Label smoothing 0.06

backlog.spec: Increase LABEL_SMOOTHING from 0.09 to 0.12.
backlog.title: Label smoothing 0.12

backlog.spec: Change widths block1 from 64 to 48. This is a narrower first block, so the first conv layers run faster at full resolution. Check the accuracy impact.
backlog.title: Block1 width 48

backlog.spec: Change widths block2 and block3 from 256 to 224 to reduce FLOPs by about 20 percent in the heavy blocks. Raise EPOCHS to 8.0 if needed.
backlog.title: Block2 and block3 width 224

backlog.spec: Increase block3 width from 256 to 320, which gives a wider final block at low resolution and so is cheap. Check whether the accuracy gain pays for the time.
backlog.title: Block3 width 320

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup replace nn.SiLU with nn.GELU. Compare cost; the activation is fused by compile so the time is similar.
backlog.title: Replace SiLU with GELU

backlog.spec: Raise HEAD_LR from 0.5415 to 0.7 and check for an accuracy gain.
backlog.title: Head learning rate 0.7

backlog.spec: Reduce WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS from 0.2 to 0.1. This is a minor saving of backward work for the whiten layer.
backlog.title: Whiten bias epochs 0.1

backlog.spec: Set EPOCHS=7.2 and raise MUON_LR to 0.225, trading a little accuracy for time.
backlog.title: Fewer epochs 7.2 with higher peak LR

backlog.spec: In the Muon step, keep momentum buffers in the gradient dtype to avoid creating the grad_casts list. Set momentum_buffer_dtype to torch.half but use torch._foreach_add_ with the half gradients directly, if they are already half. This reduces Python overhead per step.
backlog.title: Skip momentum fp16 casts

backlog.spec: Replace the norm_freq schedule 2 + int(15*progress) with a constant 8. This reduces the _foreach_norm work.
backlog.title: Norm scaling every 4 steps fixed

backlog.spec: Set TRANSLATE=1. This uses a smaller pad and less augmentation, which may suit a short schedule.
backlog.title: Reduce translate to 1

backlog.spec: Set TRANSLATE=3 for stronger augmentation and slightly more epochs, 8.0, to compensate.
backlog.title: Translate 3

backlog.spec: Change forward_step's torch.compile mode from max-autotune to default. This only affects compile time, not run time, but it checks whether kernel choices matter. Skip if the slot is better used elsewhere.
backlog.title: Cheaper compile mode for forward

backlog.spec: Change the TTA first pass to use mirror averaging (net(x)+net(x.flip(-1)))/2 for all test images before choosing the uncertain ones, and lower UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE to 0.15 to compensate.
backlog.title: Ensemble flipped logits in all test images

backlog.spec: Raise WEIGHT_DECAY from 1.04e-06 to 3e-06 and check for regularization benefit.
backlog.title: Weight decay increase

backlog.spec: Change BatchNorm default momentum parameter from 0.5566 to 0.45 so running stats track recent weights faster given the short training.
backlog.title: BatchNorm momentum 0.45

backlog.spec: Change the head output division by x.size(-1) to a division by x.size(-1)*0.8, which equals a larger logit scale. Check the effect with label smoothing.
backlog.title: Final max pool scale factor

backlog.spec: Raise SGD_MOMENTUM from 0.825 to 0.9 and lower BIAS_LR to 0.045 to keep the effective step similar.
backlog.title: Nesterov SGD momentum 0.9

backlog.spec: In train(), for the first ~35% of steps downsample each training batch to 24x24 with F.interpolate (bilinear, antialias off) before the model, then use full 32x32 afterwards. The network is fully convolutional up to the final MaxPool2d(3) and flatten, so the flatten size changes: make the final pooling adaptive (nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) equivalent at 32 res gives 3x3->1x1 after pool(3); use AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) in place of MaxPool2d(3)) so both resolutions work. Mark forward_step with dynamic=False; it will compile two shapes, which is untimed. Keep total epochs unchanged; the aim is cheaper early steps.
backlog.title: Progressive resolution early epochs

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.forward keep conv1 -> pool -> norm -> act but replace the first block's (block1 only) ordering so it is conv1 -> norm -> act -> pool? No: instead do the opposite cheaper change: apply activation before pooling is costlier, so leave it. Concretely implement: block1 conv2 is replaced by a depthwise-separable pair (3x3 depthwise conv groups=64 followed by 1x1 conv 64->64) to cut block1 FLOPs at 16x16 resolution... Muon only handles 4D params, which both are, but the depthwise weight has shape (64,1,3,3); that is fine for orthogonalisation of a 64x9 matrix. Keep dirac init off for the depthwise conv.
backlog.title: Drop the first conv's pooling order: pool after norm

backlog.spec: Change widths to block1=64, block2=256, block3=192. This lowers the cost of the last block's convs (conv1 256->192, conv2 192->192) and the head input. The head scale uses x.size(-1) so it adapts automatically. Everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Remove block3 second conv's width: 192

backlog.spec: After batch_crop in CifarLoader.__iter__ (before jitter), apply a cheap per-image random 8x8 cutout: build a boolean mask on GPU from per-image random offsets via arange comparisons (compiled with torch.compile) and multiply images by ~mask. Apply only for the first 60% of epochs (self.epoch < 5) so that the final epochs see clean images. Expect better generalisation allowing fewer epochs (try EPOCHS 7.2).
backlog.title: Mixed-in cutout style regularisation

backlog.spec: Not allowed to modify the model in predict, so instead at the end of train() average weights: keep an EMA copy of parameters and BN running stats updated every 4 steps over the last 30% of training with decay 0.9 using torch._foreach_lerp_, then copy EMA into the model at the end of train(). Use torch._foreach operations on lists of parameters and buffers to keep overhead small.
backlog.title: Lookahead-free EMA of weights for prediction

backlog.spec: Ramp MUON_MOMENTUM linearly from 0.5 at step 0 to 0.8 at the end of training by setting optimizer2.param_groups[0]['momentum'] each step in the training loop (the Muon.step reads group['momentum']). Rationale: early noisy phase benefits from less momentum while late phase benefits from smoother updates.
backlog.title: Warmup-free cosine-like LR with nonzero Muon momentum ramp

backlog.spec: Make label smoothing a function of progress: pass a tensor or python float into forward_step changing from 0.15 at start to 0.02 at the end, linearly in step. To avoid recompiles, pass it as a 0-d CUDA tensor and compute the loss manually: logp=F.log_softmax(outputs.float(),1); loss = -((1-s)*logp.gather(1,labels[:,None]).squeeze(1) + s*logp.mean(1)).sum().
backlog.title: Label smoothing decay to zero

backlog.spec: In _get_tta_logits drop the crop_br and its flipped view, using only images_batch, crop_tl and their flips (4 views instead of 6). This cuts TTA compute by a third on 25% of the test set, saving predict time; accuracy loss is expected to be tiny. Update the num_views computation (already derived from shapes).
backlog.title: Test-time TTA with one fewer view

backlog.spec: Change forward_step compile mode from 'max-autotune' to 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' is not the point; instead use torch.compile(mode='max-autotune') as is, but also compile the whole Muon update by wrapping the foreach momentum/nesterov/update code in a single torch.compile'd function taking lists of tensors (the norm scaling branch computed every step by a Python flag passed as a constant). This reduces Python and kernel-launch overhead per step, which matters at ~25 steps per epoch.
backlog.title: Channels-last bf16-free: CUDA graphs for the train step

backlog.spec: In train(), change the progressive-resolution threshold from `step < 0.35 * total_train_steps` to `step < 0.5 * total_train_steps` (24x24 inputs). Tests whether more cheap low-res steps lower time more than they cost accuracy.
backlog.title: Low-res phase 45% of steps

backlog.spec: In train(), use a three-stage resolution schedule: for step < 0.2*total_train_steps interpolate inputs to 20x20, for step < 0.5*total_train_steps to 24x24, else full 32x32. Keep the bilinear interpolate and channels_last contiguous call. Each new shape triggers one extra compile, which is not timed.
backlog.title: Lower low-res size to 20x20 early

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, remove the third unrolled quintic iteration (keep two). This saves matmul time in every Muon step. Optionally raise MUON_LR by 5%.
backlog.title: Two Newton-Schulz iterations

backlog.spec: Combine the two earlier near-noise wins: set widths block3 to 192, and fuse Muon's momentum-buffer update and Nesterov combination into one torch.compile'd helper function. Both only cut compute, so they should stack on the progressive-resolution base.
backlog.title: Block3 width 192 plus fused Muon momentum

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the conv weights, updated every 4 steps in the last 30% of training with decay 0.9, and swap it in for predict. Must not modify the model inside predict(). Instead, copy the EMA weights into the model at the end of train(). Could give an accuracy gain for low cost.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for prediction

backlog.spec: Add a batched random cutout of 8x8 zeroed on the normalised images, applied to half the samples in the loader, inside a compiled function like batch_color_jitter. Raising regularisation could permit fewer epochs (EPOCHS 7.0) at the same accuracy.
backlog.title: Cutout regularisation, small patches

backlog.spec: Set EPOCHS=7.0 and add a linear LR warmup over the first 5% of steps for the Muon and SGD groups (multiply lr_factor2 by min(1, step/(0.05*total))). Aims to retain accuracy while shortening the run.
backlog.title: Fewer epochs with warmup

backlog.spec: Replace SiLU with GELU everywhere in ConvGroup (self.activ = nn.GELU()). GELU is already used after whitening, so fewer distinct kernels exist, and it may be slightly faster in the compiled graph.
backlog.title: Drop second-conv BN in block1 at low res

backlog.spec: In _get_tta_logits, use base_views = cat([images_batch, crop_br]) with flipped views (4 views instead of 6). This lowers predict time while the TTA is still applied to the 25% least confident images.
backlog.title: Reduce TTA to mirror plus one shift

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 2048 and scale BIAS_LR and HEAD_LR by about 1.2x (MUON_LR by 1.1x). Keep EPOCHS 7.65. Larger batches give fewer optimizer steps, so less Muon and Python overhead per epoch. WEIGHT_DECAY is multiplied by batch size inside train(), so keep the product wd constant by scaling WEIGHT_DECAY by 1536/2048.
backlog.title: Batch 2048 with scaled LRs

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 1024 and EPOCHS to 7.2. Scale WEIGHT_DECAY by 1536/1024 so wd (WEIGHT_DECAY * batch) stays constant. Lower BIAS_LR and HEAD_LR by about 10%. More steps may improve accuracy per epoch, which would offset the extra optimizer overhead.
backlog.title: Batch 1024 with 7.2 epochs

backlog.spec: Change the low-res threshold in the training loop from 0.35 to 0.45 of total_train_steps (24x24 bilinear). Everything else stays the same. This tests whether more cheap low-res steps shift the time-accuracy tradeoff favorably.
backlog.title: Low-res phase 45% with 20x20 start-free

backlog.spec: Use a two-stage progressive resolution schedule: 24x24 for the first 30% of steps, 28x28 (bilinear, antialias=False) for the next 30%, then full 32x32. Add the new interpolate branch in the training loop. Each distinct shape triggers one extra untimed compile, which is fine.
backlog.title: Low-res size 28 for late phase ramp

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA of the model parameters and BN buffers, updated every 4 steps with decay about 0.9 during the last 40% of training. At the end of train(), copy the EMA weights into the model. Use torch._foreach_lerp_ on the parameter lists for speed. Measure whether accuracy gains outweigh the small overhead.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for prediction

backlog.spec: Set WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS to 0.1 and HEAD_LR to 0.7 in one change. This shortens the whiten-bias training phase and speeds up head learning. Both are small constants.
backlog.title: Whiten bias epochs 0.1 and head LR 0.7

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.__init__, set self.activ = nn.GELU() instead of nn.SiLU(). The whitening front already uses GELU, so this tests whether the cheaper or different activation helps speed or accuracy under torch.compile.
backlog.title: Replace SiLU with GELU in ConvGroup

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.forward, apply norm1 before pool (conv, norm, pool, activ) instead of (conv, pool, norm, activ). Normalisation before max pool is a different function and may change accuracy slightly. In the first block it costs more memory traffic but changes the statistics. Test the accuracy and time effect.
backlog.title: Skip BN on second conv's first-block at low res: pool-after-norm order

backlog.spec: Set TRANSLATE from 2 to 1. The smaller pad shrinks the cached padded image and gather cost, and less translation may suit a short 7.65-epoch schedule. Check the TTA code still works, since it uses its own pad=1.
backlog.title: Translate 1 augmentation

incumbent.description: Train the first 35% of steps at 24x24 resolution (bilinear downsample) with an adaptive final max pool, then switch to full 32x32.

memo: Twenty slots used, all single-run (noise sd about 0.026). Only slot 6 was accepted: 24x24 for the first 35% of steps gave -0.1139 official. Resolution schedules around it did not beat it: slot 13 (three-stage) -0.0963, slot 19 (24 then 28) -0.0789. Slot 17 (TRANSLATE 1) scored -0.1303 and slot 9 (fused Muon update) -0.1223 and slot 7 (block3 width 192) -0.1203. All are slightly better in raw cost than the incumbent but within noise, so they are unconfirmed. Slot 14 (7 + 9 combined) scored -0.0361, so gains may not stack. Failures: TTA changes (slots 0, 2, 3, 18), removing jitter (0.0454), cutout (0.0956), a third-iteration removal in Muon (0.3361), extra weight decay, label smoothing decay, and narrower blocks 1 and 2. Next: replicate slot 17, then slot 9, each on the 24x24 base. Then try combining only the ones that replicate. Look for cheap per-step savings. Avoid TTA, width and regularization tweaks.
